newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks firm after soft opening.
newsitem.headline: French stocks firm after soft opening.

text.p: French shares turned higher on Monday, helped by a fresh poll showing the conservatives ahead, after a weak start in low volume due to London's market holiday, traders said.
The bourse drew support from a BVA opinion poll showing the UDF/RPR and other conservative parties could win 294 seats in the parliamentary elections.
That showed an increase for the right over weekend polls showing the Socialist party reducing the conservatives' lead.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 6.28 points or 0.24 percent at 2,661.59 at 0835 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 15 at 2,653 from Friday's close.
The market, which rose five percent last week, should be supported by Friday's surge on bond markets and Wall Street after a U.S. agreement on a balanced budget, a broker said.

He added he thought it was unlikely last Thursday's landslide win by the Labour party in the British parliamentary election would sway French voters. "I don't think there will be a big impact on the outcome of the French election," he said.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on the radio this morning the election race was getting closer: "I have always thought the vote would be close."
Political risk has restricted trading volumes, traders said.
Dollar earners and firms trading in Asia where Hong Kong and Singapore dollars are linked to the U.S. currency should benefit from the unit's steady tone.
Among them were Air Liquide, up 0.81 percent at 871 francs, Michelin, up 1.43 percent at 333.5, and LVMH, up 0.35 percent at 1,420.
With market volume thin, professionals were able to pick stocks and push prices around easily, said another broker.
Paribas was up 2.19 percent at 368.5, Sanofi up 1.96 percent at 571 and Accor up 2.34 percent at 875.
